correctness.rationale: Local degree 3 forces positive integer cross-color neighbor counts and k<=4. The two-column complement forces u_(i+2)=J u_i at four colors, with precise 24 seeds and 4 divisibility. At three colors, the missing-color recurrence over F3 entails u_(i+3)=J u_i, 36 admissible seeds at 6-divisible lengths and exactly 6 diagonal seeds at odd 3-multiples. Regularity requires n divisible by 3. The layer-constant two-color construction covers remaining cases; no color-surjectivity ambiguity remains. Independently enumerated finite neighbor distributions verify 36 ordered (n,k) instances.

originality.rationale: The closest full-text FAT paper (Beers--Mulas, arXiv:2604.21665, Section 7, Theorem 7.6/Fig. 9) already contains the Cartesian lifting of a three-color FAT coloring of C_6 to C_6 square K_2. That existential example is excluded from novelty. Its theorem does not classify maximal FAT k for every prism length or count 3-/4-colorings. An explicit rigid four-period and six-period classification with full exact named-color census does not follow as a stated corollary of the cited lifting result. Searches of other FAT papers and alternate graph-cover/quotient-matrix terms revealed no direct complete classification; residual historical-priority risk is retained.
residual_risks: General perfect-coloring/equitable-partition/classical graph-cover literature may classify these prisms under different names; targeted searches do not exclude hidden or unpublished priority.
Not every related graph-covering paper could be comprehensively inspected; some alternate-host papers were read only by abstract.
The exact census has not undergone an independent historical-priority review.

value.rationale: A complete two-parameter (n,k=3,4) named census and exact maximum k for the natural infinite circular-ladder prism family, producing sharp interacting mod-3/mod-4 congruence classes. Four- and six-period layer-swap rigidity explain why generic product lower bounds are not sharp or complete. Exact counts identify a single unnamed four-color partition and one versus six three-color partitions, a meaningful structural refinement beyond existing examples.
